notes: Reported by Bryce: Hermes repeatedly paged 'OpenRouter is DOWN, sdlc-developer has no healthy fallback'. Confirmed FALSE — /models 200, /auth/key 200 with the live key, chat/completions 200. Root cause: HEALTH_ENDPOINTS in agents/model-manager.mjs had no openrouter entry, so pingProvider returned {up:false,error:'unknown provider'}, latching down at 2 failures (reached 255) and firing CRITICAL for all 4 agents since every fallback rung is an OpenRouter model. 7,204 all-fallbacks-down ledger events since 2026-07-05. The openrouter-provider change moved defaultProvider to OpenRouter but never added the probe, and no test checked the two stayed in sync. FIXED: /auth/key probe (free, no model tokens, model-agnostic), key resolved from ~/.hermes/.env via resolveProviderKey(), new 'unmonitored' status so a missing probe can never masquerade as an outage, poisoned providerHealth.openrouter deleted, guard test asserts every budget.json provider has a HEALTH_ENDPOINTS entry. VERIFIED: live sweep reports openrouter up (1809ms), consecutiveFailures 0, all 4 agents on real models, zero new all-fallbacks-down rows. Negative control: invalid key -> HTTP 401 -> up:false, so real outages still latch down and page. npm test 165/165, model-manager suite 54/54 (5 new), four-layer-validate PASSED, test-behavior 175/10 identical before and after (10 failures pre-existing and unrelated). OPEN: T-404 — Bryce to confirm the Telegram pages stop on the next scheduler tick. Deferred to BACKLOG #28: cross-provider fallback rungs (every rung is currently OpenRouter, so a real outage is still a total stoppage) — deliberately not bundled, since adding a working fallback would have masked this bug rather than fixed it.
